security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown backticks, JavaScript template literals, fixed repository-relative paths, and validation tooling. However, SKILL.md instructs agents to silently run an npx-based skill update before use, which can retrieve and replace content without user consent.

remediation.issue: The skill instructs agents to silently update itself through npx before performing work.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the automatic update instruction. Present updates as an optional, user-approved command with a pinned package version and explain what will change.

content.value_statement: Moving a supported Remotion composition to HyperFrames requires mapping React timing and scene logic to HTML and GSAP. This skill guides the migration, identifies unsupported patterns, and validates visual fidelity.
actual_capabilities: Classifies whether an explicit Remotion-to-HyperFrames migration request matches the skill.
Lints Remotion source for state, effects, async metadata, and unsupported React libraries.
Maps supported Remotion composition, sequencing, timing, media, transition, font, and Lottie patterns to HyperFrames guidance.
Produces guidance for an HTML composition with a paused GSAP timeline and composition metadata.
Explains how to compare Remotion and HyperFrames renders with SSIM and frame strips.
limitations: Only supports one-way migration from existing Remotion source to HyperFrames.
Does not translate interactive React state machines or effects with non-empty dependencies.
Some media behavior, custom presentations, and font choices can require approximation or manual work.
Rendering and visual comparison require the local Remotion, HyperFrames, Node.js, and FFmpeg tooling.

use_cases.title: Migrate a marketing video
use_cases.description: Convert a supported Remotion marketing composition into a seekable HyperFrames HTML animation.

use_cases.title: Assess migration readiness
use_cases.description: Lint a Remotion codebase and identify blockers before committing to a migration.

use_cases.title: Validate a conversion
use_cases.description: Compare baseline and translated renders to identify frames that need adjustment.

prompt_templates.title: Start a migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this existing Remotion composition to HyperFrames. First identify any unsupported patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Check source compatibility
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the Remotion compatibility review on this source directory and list blockers, warnings, and supported APIs.

prompt_templates.title: Translate scene timing
prompt_templates.prompt: Translate this Remotion composition into HyperFrames HTML and GSAP. Preserve scene timing, dimensions, fps, and scalar props.

prompt_templates.title: Plan visual validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a validation plan for this Remotion-to-HyperFrames migration. Include baseline rendering, SSIM comparison, frame-strip diagnosis, and translation notes.

output_examples.input: Convert a supported two-scene Remotion composition with an image, audio, and spring animation.
output: Compatibility result: supported APIs and any warnings.
Migration plan: scene timing, media mapping, and GSAP timeline structure.
Validation checklist: render both versions and compare SSIM.

output_examples.input: Review a composition that uses useState and useEffect.
output_examples.output: Migration blocked: state-driven behavior is not a deterministic HyperFrames target. The output recommends the runtime interop approach instead.

best_practices: Run the source lint before generating a translation.
Validate with equivalent dimensions, fps, and pixel format before comparing renders.
Write translation notes for every dropped, substituted, or approximated behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for a new video or a non-Remotion source.
Do not translate state-driven or effect-driven compositions after the lint reports a blocker.
Do not treat a visual preview as proof of frame-level fidelity.

faq.question: What source does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports explicit migrations from existing Remotion React composition source to HyperFrames.

faq.question: Can it create a new HyperFrames video?
faq.answer: No. New compositions should use the general HyperFrames authoring workflow.

faq.question: What happens when the source uses React state?
faq.answer: The lint treats state-driven and effect-driven patterns as blockers and recommends runtime interop.

faq.question: Does it support the reverse conversion?
faq.answer: No. The migration direction is Remotion to HyperFrames only.

faq.question: How is output quality checked?
faq.answer: Render the baseline and translation, compare SSIM, and inspect divergent frames with a frame strip.

faq.question: What tools are needed for validation?
faq.answer: Validation requires the local Remotion and HyperFrames toolchains, Node.js, and FFmpeg.
